sources.title: Peter B. Golden, Qepčāq, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct article: introduction, Qepchaq Tribes and Mongol conquest/continuity. Differentiates western Cumans, Central Asian Qipchaq-Qangli and western Siberian groups; political network was not a unified centralized state. Georgia connection and royal marital ties are supported.

sources.title: Kyra Lyublyanovics, Cuman integration and animal husbandry in 13th-16th century Greater Cumania, Hungary (2017)
sources.note: Original Acta Archaeologica Carpathica 52, pp. 259-287, directly read. P. 260 regional herding/trade; pp. 271-278 Orgondaszentmiklos households, animal remains and fracture. The latter archaeology concerns later Hungarian Cuman communities, not the independent steppe confederation. Entire paper and alternate download URLs counted as one work.

sources.title: Kyra Lyublyanovics, New Home, New Herds (2017)
sources.note: Original Archaeopress monograph read through full text mirror https://dokumen.pub/new-home-new-herds-cuman-integration-and-animal-husbandry-in-medieval-hungary-from-an-archaeozoological-perspective-9781784917524-9781784917531.html. Chapter 1, pp. 17-27, distinguishes outsider diet accounts, fourteenth-century Ibn Battuta and thirteenth-century migration. Same work mirrors have one budget. No universal all-meat diet inferred.

sources.title: Florin Curta, Eastern Europe in the Middle Ages (500-1300), chapter 10 (2019)
sources.note: Original Brill scholarly monograph read in indexed PDF and full-text mirror https://dokumen.pub/eastern-europe-in-the-middle-ages-500-1300-2-vols-9789004395190.html. Printed pp. 175-176: portable felt dwellings in external accounts, documentary/archaeological wagons and named strongholds. Robert de Clari may not have personally observed Cumans; stereotype flagged.

sources.title: Archaeological Museum in Krakow, the Cuman baba from Stadnytsya
sources.note: Direct museum text: twelfth/thirteenth-century female statue, caftan, hat, fabric-covered felt rolls, earrings, necklace, waist pouch and vessel. Donated in early twentieth century by Ernest Rohozinski; not a modern controlled excavation. Face details removed for unknown reasons.

sources.title: Neues Museum, Cuman statue with helmet, breastplate and riding boots
sources.note: Museum-authored Google Arts and Culture record, Museum fur Vor- und Fruhgeschichte, IIId 9031/2, twelfth-thirteenth century. Statues on conspicuous steppe locations; vessels interpreted as deceased participation in shared drinking. Interpretation is attributed, not asserted as proven universal belief.

sources.title: Warren T. Woodfin, Yuriy Rassamakin and Renata Holod, Foreign Vesture and Nomadic Identity (2010)
sources.note: Ars Orientalis 38, pp. 155-186. Original JSTOR abstract and indexed author-uploaded article https://www.researchgate.net/publication/282194639 read. Early-thirteenth-century burial dating is the authors’ proposal. Pp. 169-171: marten linings, patchwork imported silks, different weaves/dyes and older reused cloth. Burial identity not treated as a securely named khan.

sources.title: D. N. MacKenzie, Codex Cumanicus, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct scholarly entry: Latin script, 82 paper leaves, approximately 20 by 14 cm; dictionary and German-speaking monks’ grammatical/religious section. Copied 1303 first-line date does not date all manuscript contents; compilation early fourteenth century. Petrarch provenance statement is not used; provenance was not investigated here.

sources.title: Veneto manuscript catalogue, Venezia Marciana Lat. Z. 549 (=1597)
sources.note: Indexed institutional catalogue directly checked through search; direct page opening failed. Catalogue dates manuscript 1330, 82 leaves, Latin/Persian/Cuman parts and later additions. Used only to contextualize surviving copy in fourteenth century, not to give an exact date to every riddle.

sources.title: Aynur Saydova, Examples of Folklore in Codex Cumanicus
sources.note: Original Golden Scripts research paper directly read. Printed p. 27 / PDF page 13 gives normalized Cuman Ak küyməniŋ avzu yox. Ol, yumurtka. and English meaning A white tent has no mouth. It is an egg. This is a modern scholarly transcription of a Latin-script manuscript, not a diplomatic medieval spelling. No song lyrics quoted.

proposedOverrides.name: Cuman Khanates
proposedOverrides.summary: Cuman-Kipchak regional powers, disrupted by Mongol conquest and followed by continuing communities.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One assigned exact ID only. Earlier cuman-kipchak-confederation (1100-1200) is related but its polygon extends to 105.94 E and is not silently accepted as a defensible common border. kimek-kipchak-khaganate (1000-1100) is an earlier formation with a distinct eastern outline and is not associated. Potential Cuman phase sharing requires parent review; no aliases proposed in this bundle.
batchIdentityNotes.geography: 1200 polygon spans 28.64-65.85 E, 39.69-57.20 N, Europe and western Asia. Europe chosen for canonical western Cuman record; steppe range crosses continents. No geometry correction, invented common capital or universal 1279 fall.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Fourteenth-century Codex Cumanicus, Latin script; normalized scholarly transcription clearly labelled. A later language witness after independent steppe rule, not a twelfth-century autograph.
